title: BOS-942 — a credential save that silently stores nothing fails the login instead of printing 'Logged in as'

scenes.title: Home offers [l]ogin, the device-code exchange succeeds, and the post-save read-back turns the silent no-op into a visible failure

waitFor.label: the fixture starts with no credential record, so Home offers sign-in

steps.caption: No stored record: the empty BOSS_AUTH_E2E_EMAIL leaves the e2e store unseeded, so this is a plain signed-out board.
Open the login view and start the device-code flow.

waitFor.label: the device-code exchange itself succeeds — the failure being proved is on the save, not the sign-in

steps.caption: The WorkOS side is fine. Before BOS-942 that alone was enough to print 'Logged in as dave@example.com'.

waitFor.label: the poll returned a token pair and the store reported a successful save — and login still fails, because the read-back found nothing

steps.caption: BOSS_AUTH_E2E_LOGIN_SAVE_NOOP stages the production shape: Save() returns nil and stores nothing.

expect.label: the verdict is stated in the operator's terms, not as a raw keyring error

expect.text: no credential record was found after saving
expect.label: the enumerated record_absent reason is rendered as prose — never a token, never a raw error string
the remedy names the command that shows what is actually stored
the login view is on its error phase, not its success phase

steps.caption: Failure, enumerated reason, and remedy are all on one frame — and 'Logged in as' is not.
